issues.rule: Derived cache invalidated before its source is updated (logic checklist 30; conditions and predicates)
issues.problem: addExcludedMetricIfNotExists sets allMetrics = null inside the computeIfAbsent mapping function, which runs before ConcurrentHashMap inserts the new entry. Trigger: thread A calls counter("excluded.x") for the first time and nulls the cache. Before A's computeIfAbsent returns, thread B calls getMetrics(), rebuilds the snapshot from excludedMetrics (which does not yet contain the entry) and stores it in allMetrics. A then inserts the entry and nothing invalidates again. getMetrics() keeps returning a map without the excluded metric until some unrelated register() or remove() happens. That defeats the documented purpose of getMetrics(), which is to include excluded metrics so they are not re-registered. register() is not affected because it invalidates again after registerInternal returns; the counter/histogram/meter/timer/gauge paths are.
issues.fix: Invalidate after the insert. Call excludedMetrics.computeIfAbsent(...) first, and when it newly added the entry, set allMetrics = null after it returns. For example, record a flag in the mapping lambda, then invalidate once computeIfAbsent has returned. This also removes the synchronized block from inside the CHM mapping function.

also_fixes.fix: Call computeIfAbsent first, and invalidate allMetrics after it returns (only when the metric was newly added, for example by tracking that inside the mapping function). That way a snapshot taken after the invalidation sees the entry.

Invalidate after the map insert. Call excludedMetrics.computeIfAbsent(...) without side effects, then do `synchronized (this) { allMetrics = null; }` after it returns. Skip the invalidation if the returned instance was not newly created, or invalidate unconditionally, which is harmless. This also removes the monitor acquisition from inside the ConcurrentHashMap bin lock.

Invalidate after the insert: call excludedMetrics.computeIfAbsent(...) with a pure mapping function, and if the returned instance is the newly created one (or simply always when the key was absent), then synchronized(this){ allMetrics = null; }. Alternatively do the put and the invalidation in one synchronized block on the same lock getMetrics() uses, or use a version counter compared when publishing the rebuilt map.

Do the invalidation after computeIfAbsent returns, for example: Metric m = excludedMetrics.computeIfAbsent(name, mappingFunction); invalidate(); return m. Alternatively invalidate in a try/finally around it. Extract a shared invalidateAllMetrics() helper for the four call sites.

issues.rule: Test must be able to fail; assertions check the outcome
issues.problem: pool.submit(...) at line 338 discards the returned Future. The assertThat(registry.getMetrics()).isNotEmpty() on line 346 runs inside the task, so an AssertionError or any other exception there is swallowed by the executor and the test still passes. The assertion is also trivially true, because the calling thread has just registered a metric. The test therefore does not check what getMetrics() returns while registrations are in flight. The only real check is the single getMetrics() call after awaitTermination.
issues.fix: Collect the Futures and call get() on each, or record the Throwables in a queue and assert it is empty. Replace isNotEmpty() with an assertion that can fail under a race, for example that the map contains the metric this thread just registered.

issues.rule: Coverage of the change; timing-sensitive tests need evidence of repeated runs
issues.problem: The cache is invalidated in addExcludedMetricIfNotExists before the metric is inserted into excludedMetrics, and in register/remove only after the mutation. In the removal test (line 374) getMetrics() is called only before the threads start and after they finish, never concurrently with remove(). In the registration test each thread calls getMetrics() once, right after its own register(). A stale cache, for example one that misses an excluded metric because getMetrics() ran between the invalidation and the insert, would only show up as a lost or extra entry in the final call, and only in a rare interleaving. The test would almost always pass against a faulty invalidation order. Nothing in the PR shows repeated runs, and the 100-thread, latch-released tests are timing-sensitive.
issues.fix: Add a reader thread that loops on getMetrics() while writers register and remove. After all writers finish, assert the final map equals the expected key set. Run the test in a repeated loop (for example @RepeatedTest) or show repeated-run evidence in the PR.

issues.rule: Coverage of the change: new branches and boundaries are exercised
issues.problem: remove() was rewritten with two branches: excluded metric present, or fall back to super.remove(). It also gained a new return-value contract (true if removed). The test discards the return value and asserts only the final map sizes. It never checks that removing a missing name returns false, or that getMetrics() drops a removed excluded or included metric on the very next call. issues.rule: Lock on a private monitor, not the publicly reachable instance
issues.problem: The cache is guarded by the registry's own monitor. The registry is a public object handed to Vert.x/Dropwizard reporters, so any external code that synchronizes on it can stall getMetrics and every register/remove. This is speculative, because I found no such caller.
issues.fix: Guard the cache with a private final Object lock, or avoid the lock entirely by invalidating through an AtomicReference with compareAndSet.
issues.title: Use a private lock object instead of synchronized(this)

issues.problem: The point of the change is that getMetrics() returns a precomputed map until the registry changes. No test checks that two consecutive calls with no mutation return the same instance, or that a mutation produces a new one. A regression back to rebuilding the map on every call would pass every new test.
issues.fix: Add assertThat(registry.getMetrics()).isSameAs(registry.getMetrics()) with no mutation in between, and isNotSameAs after a register().
